oewn-01557986-a.learner: used with nouns you cannot count, to mean a large amount, a high degree, or a wide extent of something.
examples: They met several times, for there was much to be discussed.
There is not much water left in the jug.

oewn-00717144-v.learner: to come to think that something is true because of a feeling, a hunch, or reasons you cannot pin down.
examples: "So, Lizzy," said he, one day, "your sister is crossed in love, I find."
Wickham's affection for Lydia was just what Elizabeth had expected to find it.

oewn-00920843-v.learner: to settle something for certain by working it out, looking into it, testing it, or studying it.
examples: And that made the men suspect something, and then they soon found out what was the matter.
They found the total by adding the columns twice.

oewn-02253273-v.learner: to come upon something, as though by chance, or to meet with it.
examples: there would probably be found partisans of the claim to primacy of almost every one of the novels
You find that same joke in his earlier letters.

oewn-04936080-n.learner: the way in which something is done, or the way it happens.
examples: In a hurried manner he immediately began an inquiry after her health.
She longed to know in what manner he thought of her.

oewn-04917312-n.learner: the way a person acts or behaves.
examples: her voice was weak, and her manner affected

oewn-05854089-n.learner: a kind or sort of something.
examples: What manner of man would say such a thing?

oewn-00691086-v.learner: to judge or regard someone or something as being a certain way.
examples: If they believed him attached to me they would not try to part us
I rather wished than believed him to be sincere

oewn-00685199-v.learner: to take something to be true.
examples: She would not believe the story until she saw the letter herself.
I believe the weather will improve by tomorrow.

oewn-02019450-v.learner: to move out of a place, or go away from it.
examples: you will not leave the house without receiving her thanks for it
He dined with us the next day, and was to leave town again on Wednesday or Thursday.

oewn-02361226-v.learner: to put something in someone's care, so that they look after it or deal with it.
examples: "I leave it to yourself to determine," said Mr. Bennet.

oewn-02388582-v.learner: to take yourself out of a group or an activity that you belonged to or took part in.
examples: My youngest sister has left all her friends--has eloped
He left the club after ten years in it.

oewn-00027761-r.learner: in spite of anything that might point the other way; used before you admit something.
examples: She tried, however, to compose herself to answer him with patience, when he should have done.
Under such circumstances, however, he was not likely to be proof against the temptation.

oewn-00029193-r.learner: used to set one thing against another; looking at the other side of it.
examples: Mrs. Gardiner and her niece, however, did her justice, and pitied her.
The first task was easy; the second, however, took hours.
However tired she was, she finished the letter that night.
Mr. Collins is really great; far greater than anything Addison ever did
Oh, he is the handsomest young man that ever was seen!

oewn-00019801-r.learner: at all times, the whole time and on every single occasion.
examples: She was ever ready to help her sisters.

oewn-00213902-r.learner: used in front of an adjective to mean 'very'.
examples: She was ever so pleased with the news.

oewn-10352098-n.learner: a woman who has given birth to a child; also the word you use when you speak to your own mother.
examples: Their affectionate mother shared all their grief
Elizabeth made no attempt to reason with her mother, but remained quietly in the hall.

oewn-10352666-n.learner: a word used when speaking to an old woman.
examples: The soldier took the old woman's basket at the gate and said, "Let me carry this for you, Mother."

oewn-05843616-n.learner: a state of things that sets off and inspires some activity or situation.
examples: Necessity is the mother of invention.

oewn-06636668-n.learner: a written message sent to a person or to an organization.
examples: Soon after their return, a letter was delivered to Miss Bennet; it came from Netherfield.
"And have you answered the letter?"

oewn-06841868-n.learner: one of the agreed signs of the alphabet, used in writing to stand for the sounds of speech.
examples: The word "cat" has three letters.

oewn-07188040-n.learner: the exact words of something taken just as they stand, rather than what was meant by them.
examples: He obeyed the letter of the law and ignored what it was for.

oewn-10262834-n.learner: a polite word for any woman.
examples: After a short silence the lady first spoke.
Miss Bingley desired he would tell her what lady had the credit of inspiring such reflections.

oewn-10008828-n.learner: a woman with fine, well-bred manners.
examples: She behaved like a lady at every moment of the visit.

connotation.why: chosen over plain 'woman' to mark breeding and manners

oewn-10262488-n.learner: a woman who holds a noble rank in Britain.
examples: It is a pity that great ladies in general are not more like her.
